agent_priors_used: AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: a revalidation-based staleness detector has a structural blind cell, namely a value change that leaves field shape, headers, status, validator and the mechanism's own postcondition unchanged. The prevalence of that cell, not threshold tuning, is what decides whether a guard is an asset or an architectural liability. SPIDER has never measured that prevalence; Graph's own handoff names it as its materially orthogonal sub-question.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: on observational real-Web HTTP data, held-out predictability is dominated by site identity, popularity and template boilerplate. A falsifiable beyond-memory test therefore needs matched intervention structure or a comparator matched on site and action template. A permutation-only contrast on observational signatures confounds the mechanism with the site, which is exactly what the accepted C-WEB-DYNAMICS decision recorded.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: measurement instruments fail in correlated, self-fulfilling ways. A frozen decision rule whose accept region has empty interior, or whose null is invariant under the label permutation it is meant to test, produces invalid packets no matter how many times it is run. Certificate-before-experiment (a pre-execution receipt plus known-positive and known-negative controls that must be shown to fire) is therefore a distinct deliverable from instrument validation, and it is the deliverable several lanes actually need.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: long-horizon tool-agent economics are dominated by the accounting convention, and per-workflow versus per-task versus per-compilation amortization moves break-even by orders of magnitude. The binding input to any honest amortization claim is the recurrence of the carried state against reuse count, not the elegance of the mechanism. SPIDER has never measured that recurrence and has never found it published.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: retrieval and memory baselines for tool agents are strong. An inheritance-beyond-memory claim tested only against cold re-derivation is close to unfalsifiable and its positive is uninteresting; the discriminating comparison is against a strong retrieval baseline at equal accuracy and equal budget.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: shared frozen vocabularies produce correlated instrument failure across packets, because every lane inherits the same gate. One shared, demonstrably discriminating identity gate fixes a family of failures; per-experiment retries with better search queries do not.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: when a break-even is analytically forced to infinity by the frozen cost model, the object under test is the cost model, not the world. Reading that as a cheap-regime economic negative inverts the direction of inference and is how a design defect becomes a false product conclusion.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: substrate bring-up must be idempotent and receipt-certified. When each lane re-implements bring-up, failures cluster on health gates (unbound routes, missing validators, missing cross-worker signals) and burn entire cycles; when one lane owns a certified contract with a machine-checkable pre-execution receipt, the failure mode moves to science.

AGENT PRIOR, not SPIDER evidence: parallel lanes given adjacent mandates tend to converge on the same question through different vocabulary. Causal orthogonality between lanes has to be asserted explicitly in the mandate or it will not happen.

allocation.comparative_reasoning: Against CONTINUE on C-PARAM-INHERIT with the identifier-level support model as the parent handoff proposes: rejected, and the reasons are comparative rather than stylistic. That question is fundamental micro-research on a Graph-owned claim, it is the third consecutive packet in Product's recent basin, the incumbent binder is being reverted anyway so the comparison would be against code in flux, and Graph can implement competing support models without touching the incumbent, which is a strictly better test of independence. Against the full end-to-end M_total_f10 Pareto gate on C-PRODUCT-ECON: I agree it must wait, because the accepted record shows its honest accounting requires the freshness, repair and parameterization primitives, whose break-evens currently rest on a per-task rate that is exactly the predecessor packet's abstention count and on a disputed induction budget differing by a factor of nine between two prereg sections; running it now would reproduce that defect at larger scale. Against parking Product until C-FRESHNESS and C-DELTA-REPAIR mature: that leaves the product lane dormant for an unbounded time while three claims churn, which is the silent-dormancy failure the direction policy exists to prevent, and it wastes the one lane that can test the thesis end to end. Against deferring everything to Graph and running no Product experiment: the external-agent arm cannot be delegated, because no other lane owns end-to-end economics.

allocation.question: First, discharge the standing obligation recorded in the accepted verdict: revert the committed four-file 1466-line insertion-variability kernel delta from the Product branch while retaining the evidence packets, per Automation invariant 13; this is hygiene, not an experiment, and it must be recorded as done. Then, on the product thesis itself: does a real external agent with a real LLM benefit from SPIDER's inherited mechanisms beyond strong memory and instruction baselines, at equal model, tools and budget? The frozen design must, before anything else, produce a SUBSTRATE-AND-CAPABILITY READINESS CERTIFICATE and terminate MEASUREMENT_INVALID at that gate if any element is absent, rather than substituting a synthetic proxy: a reachable model endpoint, a task set of at least thirty credential-free real-Web tasks whose success postconditions are mechanically verifiable rather than self-reported, and per-trajectory honest counters instrumented and DEMONSTRATED to fire by way of a seeded accounting-fidelity control. Baselines are executed and validated FIRST, before the SPIDER arm, because the entire scientific content of any positive is relative to them: cold re-derivation with no stored knowledge, instructions-only with no retrieval and no inheritance, and retrieval over the same observations at matched budget, with retrieval quality reported and not assumed. SPIDER's arm inherits mechanisms as it actually can today, and the packet must declare, before freeze and not after, exactly which inheritance primitives are absent from that arm, namely any freshness guard and any delta repair, so that a null is read as a lower bound on the product thesis rather than as a refutation of it. Primary readout is end-to-end cost per verified success with accuracy reported alongside it and never traded against it silently, plus false accepts and abstentions counted as costs; the falsifier requires the SPIDER arm to beat retrieval at matched budget and matched accuracy, and a SPIDER loss to retrieval at equal accuracy is an admissible and highly decision-relevant outcome that would retire the retrieval-versus-inheritance architecture question in favour of retrieval. Both outcomes move the product: a win supplies the first product-level evidence in the program, and a loss supplies the first reason to stop building inheritance on this substrate class.
allocation.rationale: C-LLM-INHERIT is the program's actual product thesis, it has 24 experiments and no admissible evidence, both its owner lanes have it on their neglected list, and no other lane can own it: it requires external-agent behaviour and end-to-end economics, which is Product's charter. Product is also IDLE, flagged for a local attractor, and has just run two consecutive packets on C-PARAM-INHERIT and C-PRODUCT-ECON micro-economics, both of which produced valid measurement under a defective design. Putting the identifier-level support model back into Product, as the Scout proposes, would be a third consecutive packet in the same basin and would duplicate Graph, which is where that mechanism question belongs. The deeper reason for the pivot is that Product has been measuring the economics of inheritance components in isolation while the component that determines whether the product exists has never been measured at all: whether an actual agent is actually better off. I accept the real risk that this experiment returns MEASUREMENT_INVALID, because model access, mechanically verifiable postconditions and honest counters have each defeated prior attempts. What I do not accept is the alternative of another isolation-level economics packet: that path reliably produces valid measurement of things that do not decide the product. The readiness certificate is the direct counter to the program's dominant pathology, because it converts a missing substrate into a cheap, honest, early abort instead of an expensive invalid packet, and because the strong-baseline-first ordering means that even a failed SPIDER arm would still yield the first valid execution of retrieval-K5 and instructions-only baselines against a real agent, which is itself an unheld external comparator.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: SPIDER's dominant pathology this cycle is not falsification, it is unmeasurability. Of 414 canonical experiments, the recent window is overwhelmingly MEASUREMENT_INVALID, and not one claim has moved above EXPERIMENTAL in this window. Reading the accepted decisions closely, the failures cluster into four distinct and separately fixable classes, and conflating them is what has been driving the lanes deeper into the same basins. (1) FROZEN-DESIGN DEFECTS, where the design itself cannot execute the intended inference: an accept region with an empty interior, a PC threshold arithmetically outside the metric's dynamic range, a count-preserving relabel null that is invariant by construction, a frozen calibration anchor that was factually wrong at freeze, an identity gate whose keyword vocabulary was taken from the positive control and is therefore anti-correlated with the construct being screened, and a product gate whose scoring makes it maximised by refusing everything unseen. These are design defects and each is cheaply preventable by requiring pre-freeze attainability proofs, power checks and a demonstrated-firing null. (2) SUBSTRATE NOT ACTUALLY BROUGHT UP, where the packet reaches its health gate with routes unbound, no ETag 304s, no cross-worker pid spread, or a browser that was never provisioned; Graph's four C-FRESHNESS/C-DELTA-REPAIR invalidations are this class, and the evidence says the guard logic is not the blocker. (3) INSTRUMENT-LANE CONFUSION, where a lane spends its cycle validating a measurement instrument while its own scientific claim gets no admissible evidence: twelve consecutive Physics packets on C-WEB-DYNAMICS, 82 experiments on that claim, still HYPOTHESIS. (4) PROGRAM-LEVEL CONTROL DEFECTS that no lane owns and no lane can repair: the V9_CODE_HASHED_INTO_FREEZE gate has made C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE unsatisfiable by construction for three consecutive experiments, because the freezer hashes only request/spec/prereg and the scope checker gives DESIGN empty prefixes. I record this as an escalation: it is a control-plane repair, it is outside every lane's allowed code roots, and I cannot make it myself under my own branch discipline. Until it is repaired by the repository owner, no further C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE experiment should be dispatched; the cost of continuing to try is three-to-one wasted packets against a claim at 25 experiments. The strategic consequence for this cycle is a deliberate re-ordering of attention. The program's central question is whether cumulative operational inheritance beats cold re-derivation and strong retrieval for an external agent on the real Web, under honest per-trajectory cost. That question is blocked not by lack of hypotheses but by the absence of three things that nobody currently owns as deliverables: a substrate other lanes can bind against without re-paying bring-up cost and dying, a set of validly executed real-Web observables, and the recurrence/break-even specification that decides whether cross-episode inheritance has an amortization surface at all. My allocation therefore pushes three lanes onto those three objects (Runtime to substrate certification and cross-lane portability; Frontier to real-Web state stationarity and re-acquisition cost; Intel to the recurrence and amortization-anchor determination) and moves the two remaining idle lanes onto the neglected central claims rather than onto further instrument work (Graph to the C-PARAM-INHERIT registry gate, which is the only untouched gate on the program's highest-status claim; Product to C-LLM-INHERIT, the product thesis itself, which has 24 experiments and no admissible evidence and which no other lane can own). Two obligations are named rather than allocated, because they are not experiments: Product must revert the committed four-file 1466-line kernel delta recorded as scheduled-for-revert in the accepted verdict, per Automation invariant 13, and the V9 control-plane repair above must be escalated. Finally, a caution about the shape of this portfolio. Five of six lanes currently have a live or frozen transaction or a fresh mandate, which is correct for one cycle. If the next two cycles also produce MEASUREMENT_INVALID without any claim moving, the correct global reading is that the program's binding constraint is substrate and instrument certification rather than idea generation, and the right response is to consolidate measurement rather than to widen the search.
director_mandate.scout_assessment: The Scout brief was materially accurate on the failure taxonomy and I adopted four of its recommendations: execute Intel's Part B break-even determination from the hash-pinned source rather than running a fourth external comparator search; preserve and complete the frozen Runtime intervention-validity transaction rather than redirecting it; do not launch further compilation-bypass variants until the cross-episode binding-key defect is solved; and treat the scheduled revert of the Product kernel delta as a real obligation. I diverged in four places, on the Codex rather than on taste. First, I do not accept the recommendation to PARK the Physics predictive-accuracy program on the grounds of twelve invalid packets. Those twelve are instrument failures with named causes, and treating them as a bounded negative would close a claim that the evidence has never touched; worse, the Scout's own replacement (an intervention-validity calibration contract on constructed banks) duplicates Runtime's certified instrument work rather than advancing C-WEB-DYNAMICS, which has 82 experiments and no admissible evidence. I instead PIVOT Physics onto interventional effect factorization, which is the first option on that claim's own registry next_gate and which none of the 82 experiments has done. Second, I do not put the identifier-level support model in Product. That question is mechanism micro-research on a Graph-owned claim, and Product has now run two consecutive packets on it, both of which produced valid measurement under a defective design; a third would deepen a local attractor rather than test a claim. I assign it to Graph, where it can be implemented without touching the incumbent kernel, and give Product the neglected product thesis instead. Third, I reject the suggestion that all other lanes be explicitly gated on the outcome of the single frozen Runtime experiment. That would concentrate the entire program on one unvalidated instrument at exactly the moment the program's failure mode is unexecutable substrate. Instead I split Runtime's mandate so that Graph's and Physics' next experiments run on substrates already demonstrated executable (a proven synthetic substrate and credential-free public HTTP respectively), and only the substrate-portability contract depends on the oracle result. Fourth, I bind the pending Frontier stationarity experiment to C-WEB-DYNAMICS' timescales axis rather than leaving it ambiguously attached to C-CROSSSITE, which both matches what it actually measures and gives Physics a shared live claim while preventing the two lanes from colliding on the same object. One limitation I record explicitly: the Scout's external findings, WebArena-Verified v2 at 812 tasks, WebGym at 292k, the Stagehand selector-cache baseline and the WebChoreArena numbers, are external and not SPIDER evidence. I used them only to specify which baselines SPIDER must be compared against, I did not independently verify them this cycle, and the Stagehand-derived comparator is assigned to Intel for exactly that verification rather than adopted on the Scout's authority.

inherited_next_question: This packet's own frozen design contains the contradiction that matters, and it is a design defect rather than a null result: the ONLY never-observed collection in the test set ('widgets') is scored as a semantic false-accept every time it is bound, so the frozen semantic-guard metric is maximized by a binder that abstains on every collection it has not seen, and there is no task anywhere in the 10000 raw rows in which binding an unobserved collection is the correct answer. The packet therefore measures REFUSAL, not the TRANSFER that C-PARAM-INHERIT's registry next_gate demands ('learn on resource A, succeed on never-observed B'). The next question: on this same proven substrate class, which is one of only two that have actually produced valid measurement in the program and needs no Docker, browser, model key or external site, CAN ANY SLOT-BINDER SATISFY BOTH OBLIGATIONS AT ONCE -- binding a collection that appears in ZERO training observations at a rate that beats the declared-vocabulary incumbent and the three structural nulls, WHILE holding the semantic false-accept at or below 0.10 on a well-formed identifier that is unjustifiable for the requested collection (a well-formed sibling of a different collection requested inside a seen one, where binding is REQUIRED and the sibling is wrong) -- with (i) an IDENTIFIER-LEVEL rather than collection-level support model compared head to head (closed set over observed collection values; shape and prefix family over identifier values; cross-collection prefix transfer; explicit no-evidence UNKNOWN), each scored on the unseen-collection binding rate AND the sibling-identifier false-accept rate SIMULTANEOUSLY so neither can be bought by refusing, with family-blocked, site-grouped uncertainty and non-degenerate interval width obtained by widening the identifier distribution rather than by adding arms; (ii) an explicit measurement of whether the incumbent's 1.0 rate of executing well-formed identifiers of an unobserved collection persists when the collection is SEEN and the identifier is a well-formed sibling of another collection, which is the residual risk a collection-level closed set does not cover and which no row in this packet tests, since every recorded abstention reason concerns slot s0; (iii) the abstention rate treated as a DESIGN PARAMETER AND A COST rather than a benefit, with the break-even against within-episode reuse and against retrieval-K5 re-reported at a product-plausible near-zero out-of-support request rate as well as at the frozen 50 percent, and with the induction budget reconciled between prereg 4.2 and 4.3 BEFORE any break-even is read; and (iv) as preconditions, the frozen decision rule repaired so the degeneracy guard cannot fire on a treatment arm or on a construction-perfect baseline and so F1-F4 are evaluated before it, the A4 tie rule fixed or the Frame-R primary designation swapped for Frame B with the non-discrimination documented, and freeze extended to bind a code hash so F8 is evaluable. Either outcome changes product architecture: a support model that admits unseen collections without admitting unjustifiable siblings is the induction principle C-PARAM-INHERIT, C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE and C-CROSSSITE all stand on, and a demonstration that no such model exists on this substrate is a bounded architectural negative that closes a design, not the search domain.
